messages.subject: Re: boxplot overlay
parts:
Sorry, there's no need to reshape the data. This code seems to work:

library(ggplot2)

open in Excel:  copy to clipboard:

field<-read.delim(file="clipboard")
field$Meas.Date<-as.Date(field$Meas.Date,"%m/%d/%Y")
field$Plot.Date<-as.Date(field$Plot.Date,"%m/%d/%Y")

ggplot(field,aes(Meas.Date,Mean,colour=Region,group=Field.No))+geom_line()+geom_boxplot(aes(Plot.Date,Mean,group=interaction(Plot.Date,Region),colour=Region))

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: boxplot overlay
parts:
> Using the data and code below, I have created two plots that I would
> like to overlay.  The first plot is a "profile" plot, and is meant to
> convey the average salinity values for individual fields tracked
> through time in two different study regions (hence the two colors).
> It may turn out that I need to separate the data, and plot the red and
> blue data in their own graphs.  However, it is the parallel-ness of
> the lines from one sampling event to another that was found to be
> statistically high (the correlation between any two consecutive
> sampling events was found to be approx. equal to 0.8, or in other
> words as a group (red or blue) their values either went collectively
> up, down or remained roughly the same)

To start, I'd recommend using lubridate for date parsing, and making a
plot that captures the essence of your display, without worrying about
all the fiddly details - that's much easier to play around with.
Here's my version:

library(lubridate)

dat.boxplot$Plot_date <- mdy(dat.boxplot$Plot_date)
dat.boxplot$Measurement_Date <- mdy(dat.boxplot$Measurement_Date)

ggplot(dat.boxplot, aes(Measurement_Date, log10(ECe_mean), colour = Region)) +
geom_line(aes(group = Field_Number), alpha =1/4, size = 0.5) +
geom_boxplot(aes(Plot_date, group = interaction(Plot_date,Region)))

> 1)  The only question I have for the first plot is this:  Is there way
> to assign different alpha values based on the value of "Region"?
Are you sure you want to? I don't think this will help the display.

> The second plot gives boxplots meant to summarize, or call attention
> to, each sampling event's summary statistics.  However, there are a
> couple of difficulties with it:
>
> 1)  I need to fix the box width, much like the "width" argument in the
> standard R boxplot command.  I wasn't able to find the answer I was
> looking for at: http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/geom_boxplot.html.  How might
> I do this?
It doesn't look like it's possible, due to a bug in geom_boxplot.

> 2)  I tried placing a "fill" command in the second plot, but no matter
> where I tried it, it would work.  Where would I add the fill command
> to play around with filling in the boxes?

You want to map fill to a variable, so you need to add it into the
aesthetic mappings:

ggplot(dat.boxplot, aes(Measurement_Date, log10(ECe_mean))) +
geom_line(aes(group = Field_Number, colour = Region), alpha =1/4,
size = 0.5) +
geom_boxplot(aes(Plot_date, group = interaction(Plot_date,Region),
fill = Region))
> 3)  Is there a way to make the line's of each box thicker?

ggplot(dat.boxplot, aes(Measurement_Date, log10(ECe_mean))) +
geom_line(aes(group = Field_Number, colour = Region), alpha =1/4,
size = 0.5) +
geom_boxplot(aes(Plot_date, group = interaction(Plot_date,Region),
fill = Region), size = 2)

> 4)  Is there something analogous to staplewex (from the standard R
> boxplot function call) in geom_boxplot()?  Again, I could find an
> answer to this from http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/geom_boxplot.html

> 5)  How do I overlay the plots?  I strongly suspect it will not look
> good at first, but I'm hoping that through color manipulation, alpha
> manipulation, etc. that it will clean up nicely.

See above.

That said, I think you'd be better off using facetting for this plot:

ggplot(dat.boxplot, aes(Measurement_Date, log10(ECe_mean))) +
geom_line(aes(group = Field_Number), colour = "grey50", alpha = 1/4) +
geom_boxplot(aes(Plot_date, group = Plot_date)) +
facet_grid(Region ~ .)

Thank you very much Hadley, the code you included at the end of your
post was great. Faceting improved the plot big time. I've since been
massaging it a bit more trying to get labels to show up in clear
way.

I found that I could use the text argument with the graphics device
that is open in R, but if I try to use with an open graphics device as
in the code below I get the error message "plot.new has not been
called yet"

Searching here and over at http://r.789695.n4.nabble.com/R-help-f789696.html
didn't help me much. Hopefully this is my last hurdle...

Thanks, Eric

png(filename="c:/temp/
Plot_of__Profiles_For_Both_Regions.png",width=1350,height=900,res=120)
ggplot(dat.boxplot, aes(Measurement_Date,
log10(ECe_mean),colour=Region)) +
geom_line(aes(group = Field_Number), alpha = 1/3) +
scale_colour_manual(values=c("blue","red")) +
geom_boxplot(aes(Plot_date, group = Plot_date)) + xlab("") +
ylab(expression(paste(log[10]," ",EC[e]," dS/m"))) + ylim(0,1.4) +
facet_grid(Region ~ .) + scale_x_date(major="4 months",format="%b")
+
